passages.text: Therefore, since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
passages.sermon:
You have been raised with Christ.
Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Seek the things that are above.
Strive for what is above, where Christ is.
passages.original: Εἰ οὖν συνηγέρθητε τῷ Χριστῷ τὰ ἄνω ζητεῖτε οὗ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ καθήμενος

passages.text: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to Christians who had been raised with Christ.
He told them to focus on things above.
He said, “Set your minds on things above.”
He told them not to focus on earthly things.
He said, “Do not set your minds on earthly things.”
passages.original: τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖτε μὴ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
passages.sermon:
You are believers in Christ.
You died to your old life.
God has hidden your new life.
Your new life is with Christ.
Your new life is in God.
passages.original: ἀπεθάνετε γάρ καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν κέκρυπται σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ ἐν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
passages.sermon:
Christ is your life.
Christ will appear.
You will also appear with Christ.
You will appear with Christ in glory.
passages.original: ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν τότε καὶ ὑμεῖς σὺν αὐτῷ φανερωθήσεσθε ἐν δόξῃ

passages.text: Put to death, therefore, the components of your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
passages.sermon:
You belong to Christ.
You have died to your old life.
Your new life is hidden with Christ in God.
Therefore, put to death the parts of your earthly nature.
Put to death sexual immorality.
Put to death impurity.
Put to death lust.
Put to death evil desires.
Put to death greed.
Greed is idolatry.
passages.original: Νεκρώσατε οὖν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς πορνείαν ἀκαθαρσίαν πάθος ἐπιθυμίαν κακήν καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν ἥτις ἐστὶν εἰδωλολατρία

passages.text: Because of these, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and just.
God has wrath against sin.
Certain actions bring God’s wrath.
These actions include sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed.
God’s wrath comes because of these sins.
God’s wrath comes on the sons of disobedience.
The sons of disobedience are people who reject God and live in these sins.
passages.original: δι’ ἃ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας

passages.text: When you lived among them, you also used to walk in these ways.
passages.sermon: You once lived among people who disobeyed God.\r\nYou also behaved as they did.\r\nYou followed the same sinful ways when you lived that life.
passages.original: ἐν οἷς καὶ ὑμεῖς περιεπατήσατέ ποτε ὅτε ἐζῆτε ἐν τούτοις

passages.text: But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Colossae.
He calls them to live as God’s chosen people.
He tells them to put aside sinful behaviors.
He says, “Now you must put aside all these things.”
Put aside anger.
Put aside rage.
Put aside malice.
Put aside slander.
Put aside filthy language from your lips.
passages.original: νυνὶ δὲ ἀπόθεσθε καὶ ὑμεῖς τὰ πάντα ὀργήν θυμόν κακίαν βλασφημίαν αἰσχρολογίαν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν

passages.text: Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices, and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians.
Paul tells them not to lie to one another.
They have taken off the old self.
The old self had its own practices.
They have put on the new self.
The new self is being renewed in knowledge.
The new self is renewed in the image of its Creator.
passages.original: Μὴ ψεύδεσθε εἰς ἀλλήλους ἀπεκδυσάμενοι τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον σὺν ταῖς πράξεσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸν νέον τὸν ἀνακαινούμενον εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν κατ’ εἰκόνα τοῦ κτίσαντος αὐτόν

passages.text: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
passages.sermon:
In Christ, all believers are united.
There is no Greek here.
There is no Jew here.
There is no circumcised person here.
There is no uncircumcised person here.
There is no barbarian here.
There is no Scythian here.
There is no slave here.
There is no free person here.
Christ is everything here.
Christ is in everyone here.
passages.original: ὅπου οὐκ ἔνι Ἕλλην καὶ Ἰουδαῖος περιτομὴ καὶ ἀκροβυστία βάρβαρος Σκύθης δοῦλος ἐλεύθερος ἀλλὰ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν Χριστός

passages.text: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
passages.sermon:
You are the elect of God.
God has chosen you.
You are holy.
God loves you.
Clothe yourselves with compassion.
Show kindness.
Be humble.
Be gentle.
Be patient.
passages.original: Ἐνδύσασθε οὖν ὡς ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἅγιοι καὶ ἠγαπημένοι σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ χρηστότητα ταπεινοφροσύνην πραΰτητα μακροθυμίαν

passages.text: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
passages.sermon:
God chose you.
God made you holy.
God loves you.
You belong to God’s people.
You must bear with one another.
You must forgive each other.
If anyone has a complaint against someone, forgive that person.
The Lord forgave you.
You also must forgive others.
passages.original: ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων καὶ χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς ἐάν τις πρός τινα ἔχῃ μομφήν καθὼς καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς

passages.text: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to Christians who were chosen by God.
These Christians were holy and loved by God.
Paul told them to have compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
Paul said, “Above all these virtues, put on love.”
Love joins everything together in perfect unity.
passages.original: ἐπὶ πᾶσιν δὲ τούτοις τὴν ἀγάπην ὅ ἐστιν σύνδεσμος τῆς τελειότητος

passages.text: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
passages.sermon:
Christ calls you to live as one body.
You belong to this one body.
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts.
Be thankful.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Χριστοῦ βραβευέτω ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν εἰς ἣν καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι καὶ εὐχάριστοι γίνεσθε

passages.text: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
passages.sermon:
The word of Christ must live in you richly.
You must have all wisdom.
You must teach one another.
You must warn one another.
You must use psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.
You must sing to God.
You must sing with gratitude in your hearts.
passages.original: Ὁ λόγος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐνοικείτω ἐν ὑμῖν πλουσίως ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ νουθετοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ψαλμοῖς ὕμνοις ᾠδαῖς πνευματικαῖς ἐν τῇ χάριτι ᾄδοντες ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
passages.sermon:
You are followers of Jesus Christ.
You belong to God as His people.
Whatever you do, do it in the name of the Lord Jesus.
This includes everything you say.
This includes everything you do.
Always give thanks to God the Father through Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ πᾶν ὅ τι ἐὰν ποιῆτε ἐν λόγῳ ἢ ἐν ἔργῳ πάντα ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ εὐχαριστοῦντες τῷ Θεῷ Πατρὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
passages.sermon: Wives, submit to your husbands.\r\nThis is fitting in the Lord.
passages.original: Αἱ γυναῖκες ὑποτάσσεσθε τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ὡς ἀνῆκεν ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
passages.sermon: Husbands, love your wives.\r\nDo not be harsh with your wives.
passages.original: Οἱ ἄνδρες ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ μὴ πικραίνεσθε πρὸς αὐτάς

passages.text: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
passages.sermon: Children, obey your parents in everything.\r\nThis action pleases the Lord.
passages.original: Τὰ τέκνα ὑπακούετε τοῖς γονεῦσιν κατὰ πάντα τοῦτο γὰρ εὐάρεστόν ἐστιν ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged.
passages.sermon: Fathers, do not provoke your children.\r\nIf you provoke your children, they will become discouraged.
passages.original: Οἱ πατέρες μὴ ἐρεθίζετε τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν ἵνα μὴ ἀθυμῶσιν

passages.text: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything.
Do not obey only when they are watching you.
Do not obey just to please people.
Obey with a sincere heart.
Obey with respect for the Lord.
passages.original: Οἱ δοῦλοι ὑπακούετε κατὰ πάντα τοῖς κατὰ σάρκα κυρίοις μὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοδουλίαις ὡς ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι ἀλλ’ ἐν ἁπλότητι καρδίας φοβούμενοι τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men, because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
passages.sermon:
You must serve the Lord Christ.
You must do whatever you do with your whole being.
You must work for the Lord, not for people.
You know the Lord will give you an inheritance as your reward.
You do not serve people.
You serve the Lord Christ.
passages.original: Ὃ ἐὰν ποιῆτε ἐκ ψυχῆς ἐργάζεσθε ὡς τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπὸ Κυρίου ἀπολήμψεσθε τὴν ἀνταπόδοσιν τῆς κληρονομίας τῷ Κυρίῳ Χριστῷ δουλεύετε

passages.text: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.
passages.sermon:
God judges everyone fairly.
God does not show favoritism.
If a person does wrong, God will repay that person for the wrong.
Each person receives what they deserve for their actions.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ἀδικῶν κομίσεται ὃ ἠδίκησεν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολημψία
